prov.text: The provision for credit losses, which includes a provision for losses on unfunded commitments, is a charge to earnings to maintain the ACL on loans at a level consistent with management’s assessment of expected losses in the loan portfolio at the balance sheet date. The Company also records reversals of interest on nonaccrual loans and interest recoveries directly through the provision of credit losses.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
The following table presents a comparative summary of the major components of noninterest expense for the periods indicated.

Noninterest expense decreased $1.1 million and increased $30.3 million from the linked and prior year-to-date periods, respectively. Employee compensation and benefits decreased $2.5 million from the linked quarter primarily due to a lower associate base and a reduction in variable compensation accruals, partially offset by an increase in loan, legal, foreclosure and property maintenance expenses related to OREO and loan workouts.

The increase in noninterest expense from the prior year-to-date period was primarily due to an increase in the associate base as a result of the Branch Acquisition and merit increases throughout 2025 and 2026, an increase of $5.6 million in deposit costs due to higher deposit vertical average balances, and an increase of $4.9 million in loan, legal, foreclosure and property maintenance expenses related to OREO and loan workouts included in ‘Other expense’ in the table above. Deposit costs relate to certain businesses in the deposit verticals that receive an earnings credit allowance for deposit-related services provided to us. These earnings credit allowances are impacted by, among other things, interest rates and average balances.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
The Company’s effective tax rate was 22.9% for the third quarter of 2026 and 22.0% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. This compares to the linked and prior year-to-date effective tax rate of 21.7% and 31.5%. Included in the tax expense during the prior year-to-date period is $24.1 million in transferrable tax credits that were recaptured and approximately $8.0 million of incremental tax liability attributable to the anticipated insurance proceeds from the insured recaptured credits. Excluding these items, the adjusted effective tax rate 3 was 19.4% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in the effective tax rate from the linked and prior year-to-date periods was due to an increase in state taxes.

3 Core efficiency ratio and adjusted effective tax rate are non-GAAP measures. Refer to discussion and reconciliation of these measures in the accompanying financial tables.

Net interest income.text: • Net interest income and NIM - Net interest income of $174.6 million for the third quarter of 2026 and $509.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased $5.9 million and $50.9 million from the linked and prior year-to-date periods, respectively. Compared to the linked quarter, net interest income benefitted from organic loan growth, as well as an additional day during the period. Compared to the prior year-to-date period, the increase was primarily attributable to growth in average interest-earning assets and lower rates paid on interest-bearing liabilities, partially offset by higher average balances of interest-bearing liabilities. NIM was 4.30% for the third quarter 2026 and 4.29% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 4.30% and 4.20% for the linked and prior year-to-date periods, respectively.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
The following table presents a comparative summary of the major components of noninterest income for the periods indicated.

Total noninterest income for the third quarter of 2026 was $13.2 million and $45.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease of $0.3 million and $41.9 million from the linked and prior year-to-date periods, respectively. The decrease from the linked quarter was primarily due to lower tax credit income and a $1.4 million net loss on OREO, partially offset by a $3.8 million increase in rental income from OREO and a $2.1 million net loss on sales of investment securities in the linked quarter that did not reoccur included in ‘Other income’ in the table above. Tax credit income is typically highest in the fourth quarter of each year and will vary in other periods based on transaction volumes and fair value changes. Changes in the interest rate environment had a negative impact on tax credit projects carried at fair value.

Compared to the prior year-to-date period, the decrease was primarily driven by the $32.1 million in accrued insurance proceeds that are anticipated to be received as a result of the recaptured tax credits recognized in the prior year-to-date period that did not reoccur, and a $11.5 million decrease in tax credit income.
